fit: date-seed powder and acute exercise recovery pain
assessment: The 34-person randomized exercise comparison finds an inconclusive immediate contrast and 1.65 points less pain on the 0–10 VAS at 24 hours. Seed powder and post-training discomfort are outside the frozen culinary flesh and Parkinson comparison. The protocol and biomarker report belong to the same family.

fit: oral date-flesh extracts and rat paw swelling
assessment: Date-flesh water and methanol extracts reduced rat paw swelling. A separate seed extract arm also reduced swelling. The outcome is swelling and gauged inflammation without a clinical pain result.

fit: date-flesh extract jam and rat paw swelling
assessment: The date-extract jam arm showed less swelling than the arthritic control, and combined oil formulations were separate arms. The study measures swelling and biomarkers rather than pain and does not assign whole dried fruit.

fit: aqueous date-fruit preparation and evoked heat withdrawal
assessment: The higher extract group of the convenience-allocated experiment had longer tail-flick latency. Nociceptive response and ear swelling are distinct. Inconsistent omnibus statistics and the non-Parkinson population limit interpretation.

fit: injected date-palm spathe and separate pain assays
assessment: The injected inflorescence-sheath preparation gave an inconclusive hot-plate result and a favorable highest-dose writhing result. The spathe, route and rodent phenotype differ from the frozen exposure.

fit: retained date pit and mechanical abdominal pain
assessment: A single retained foreign-body case records symptom resolution after removal. Date pits are distinct from the edible flesh and the case gives no attributable Parkinson pain comparison.

fit: retained date pit and perianal injury
assessment: The authors attribute the observed injury and pain to a retained date pit. No incidence estimate or culinary fruit intervention is available.

fit: swallowed date pit and oesophageal injury
assessment: The case records painful swallowing and critical mechanical injury after an accidentally swallowed pit. The exposure is distinct from whole dried fruit and the outcome does not establish clinical Parkinson pain direction.
